thought.text: The `pkill -f` pattern matched my own shell command line (it contained the pattern text). Let me use the bracket trick to avoid self-matching.

reasoning_content:
pkill -f "nx.*serve" — hmm, that might have matched the current shell too. Because the shell's command line contains the string "nx.*serve" as part of the pkill pattern itself! Yeah — pkill -f matches against the full command line of processes, and our bash -c command line literally contains the string "nx.*serve.*workspace.localhost". So pkill killed our own shell. Exit code 143 = SIGTERM.

I need to be careful: use a pattern that won't match itself. For example, the pkill -f "[n]x serve" trick — the brackets prevent self-matching.

action.command: pkill -f "[s]erve.mjs" 2>/dev/null; pkill -f "nx run [a-z]+:serve" 2>/dev/null; pkill -f "[d]ev-server" 2>/dev/null; sleep 3; ps aux | grep -E "[s]erve.mjs|[d]ev-server" | head -5; echo "=== done cleanup ==="; docker ps --format "{{.Names}}: {{.Status}}" | sort | head -12
